about: POST /krb5/kdc, /krb5/service, /krb5/spnego and GET /krb5/limits. Recorded against the api as it was before the family switched to the model (docs/v0.9.6/data-model.md), on api/env/docker-tests.js. Every target that gets past the pre-flight is a *.invalid name, which RFC 6761 guarantees never resolves, so a well-formed request ends in the same 502 on any machine. The messages are the smallest frames the pre-flight accepts: 6a00 (an AS-REQ) and 6e00 (a bare AP-REQ).

body.error: message is not valid base64. It must be the Kerberos request encoded as base64 or base64url; note that node decodes invalid base64 silently, so this is checked here rather than surfacing later as "not a Kerberos request".

cases.name: kdc: bytes that are not a KDC request are refused

body.error: Refusing to relay this payload: this is not a request a KDC answers: the first byte is 0x30, and it must be 0x6a (AS-REQ) or 0x6c (TGS-REQ). It looks like text — was it decoded from base64 before being sent? This endpoint carries Kerberos KDC requests, not arbitrary bytes — see api/krb5_frame.js for why that restriction exists.

cases.name: kdc: an AP-REQ is refused and pointed at /krb5/service

body.error: Refusing to relay this payload: this is not a request a KDC answers: the first byte is 0x6e, and it must be 0x6a (AS-REQ) or 0x6c (TGS-REQ). 0x6e is AP-REQ, which goes to a SERVICE rather than to a KDC — use POST /krb5/service for that. This endpoint carries Kerberos KDC requests, not arbitrary bytes — see api/krb5_frame.js for why that restriction exists.

cases.name: kdc: a declared length that does not match is refused

body.error: Refusing to relay this payload: the AS-REQ declares 5 bytes of content, so the whole message should be 7 bytes, but 2 were supplied. A message this service cannot account for is not one it will relay. This endpoint carries Kerberos KDC requests, not arbitrary bytes — see api/krb5_frame.js for why that restriction exists.

cases.name: kdc: a port outside krb5AllowedPorts is refused

body.error: Refusing to connect to port 9. This relay carries Kerberos to Kerberos ports only (88, 464, 749). It is a raw byte relay, so an unrestricted port would make it a port scanner with a caller-chosen payload. Add the port to krb5AllowedPorts if this deployment needs it.

cases.name: kdc: a boolean for the port
cases.changed: port is an integer, its text, or null in the model. Until then the relay refused true as a port that is not a number; the model now refuses it as the wrong JSON type, before the handler.

Refusing the request: `port` must be a JSON integer or a JSON string or null. GET /api-docs describes what krb5Kdc takes.

body.error: Refusing to relay this payload: this is not something a Kerberos service accepts: the first byte is 0x6a, and it must be 0x60 (a GSS InitialContextToken wrapping an AP-REQ) or 0x6e (a bare AP-REQ). 0x6a is AS-REQ, which goes to a KDC — use POST /krb5/kdc for that. This endpoint carries Kerberos AP-REQs, not arbitrary bytes — see api/krb5_frame.js for why that restriction exists.
